newsitem.title: BULGARIA: FOCUS-Bulgaria issues new banknote as lev slides.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Bulgaria issues new banknote as lev slides.

text.p: Bulgarian shopkeepers gloomily chalked up new prices on Thursday as the lev currency slumped to new lows against the dollar and the central bank unveiled a new large denomination note.
The Bulgarian National Bank (BNB) said high inflation meant a 10,000 lev note was now needed in addition to the 5,000 lev bill introduced on June 17.
The new note, depicting Bulgarian artist Vladimir Dimitrov and his work, goes into circulation on Monday.
The lev has declined from 71 to the dollar in January to 435 on the interbank market at noon on Thursday.

Price rises are taking their toll among Bulgarians, though a general strike called by one trade union organisation on Wednesday to call for a cabinet shuffle and early parliamentary elections received only token support.
"We don't have average customers any more, we have people with an awful lot of money and people with no money at all," said shop assistant Veselina Yovcheva at a city centre grocery.
"It's very awkward if someone buys imported Greek steaks and olives and spends 80,000 levs in one go and at the same time you have pensioners buying just 100 grammes of white cheese."
Even some snack stalls gave up changing individual price tags and put up a sign indicating the percentage to add.

"I don't feel that I'm running a shop any more, I feel like I'm running an exhibition. Everyone just comes in and looks, they don't even ask for the prices," said Nikolai Iliev, who runs a store selling stereo equipment.

"Most of my colleagues are closing down for a couple of weeks pretending to do repairs but in fact everyone is waiting to see how this crisis will affect their business," said snack seller Tsvetelina Ivanova, whose stall displayed a sign saying "+15 percent".
On Wednesday, the central bank said its foreign exchange reserves had fallen to $525 million at the end of November from $541 million at the end of October and $1.4 billion a year ago.

The BNB said it would continue intervening to support the lev, in an apparent attempt to give the market a positive signal, but it has sold only small quantities of dollars since the lev's slide intensified last month and dealers said it was not active on the interbank market on Thursday.

The BNB board, which was holding its weekly meeting on Thursday, said it would step up supervision to ensure that commercial banks adhere to its regulations concerning their net open foreign currency positions.

BNB governor Lyubomir Filipov has said the bank cannot both meet foreign debt payments and keep enough foreign exchange reserves to back levs in circulation under a currency board scheme expected to be introduced next year.
Bulgarian Brady bonds firmed on the prospect that Bulgaria would have access to more funding from the International Monetary Fund once a currency board is introduced.

The mechanism is a form of fixed exchange rate regime which requires that levs in circulation and commercial banks' minimum reserves at the central bank match central bank foreign exchange and gold reserves.

Two technical IMF missions are expected to arrive in Sofia next week to adjust the 1997 draft budget frame to currency board requirements and help prepare fiscal law amendments which would make the system operational.
